source_text: Meta-analyses of over 30 such studies estimated a consistent 50-70% lower HIV risk among circumcised men in high-risk groups, prompting hypotheses that circumcision biologically limits viral ingress by eliminating the foreskin's Langerhans cells—dendritic cells highly susceptible to HIV—and reducing mucosal trauma during sex. [94]
